> Summary: Improve error logging for timeouts in the HTTP client so operators can distinguish DNS failures, connection timeouts, and read timeouts, while keeping overall logging behavior consistent.
>
> Steps:
> 1. Reproduce the current behavior by running the existing HTTP client timeout tests:
>    - From the repository root, run: `pytest tests/http_client/ -k "timeout"`.

>    - Do not alter the public method signature or the return types.
>    - Follow the existing logging conventions and patterns described in the Project Contribution Guide.

>    - Timeout errors include a concise `reason` field (e.g., `"dns"`, `"connect"`, or `"read"`).
>    - The log level and logger name remain the same as the current timeout logging.
>    - No new dependencies or configuration options are introduced.
> 4. Add or update tests under `tests/http_client/test_timeouts.py` to:
>    - Verify that the appropriate `reason` string appears in log records for DNS, connect, and read timeouts.
>    - Reuse the existing log-capture helpers and patterns.
> 5. Run the HTTP client tests locally:
>    - `pytest tests/http_client/`.
>    - Fix any failures that result from your changes.
> 6. Once tests pass, open a pull request with:
>    - Title: "Improve timeout error logging in HTTP client".
>    - A description that summarizes the behavior change, references this issue, and lists the added/updated tests.
>    - Any documentation updates required by the Project Contribution Guide for changes in logging behavior.
>
> Please adhere closely to the Project Contribution Guide (logging conventions, test layout, and PR format). If any of these steps are unclear, ask for clarification before you start modifying code.

rounds.response:
Plan (concrete mapping and test sketch):

- Exception-to-reason mapping: treat socket.gaierror or OSError/EAI_* raised during name resolution as "dns"; treat connection-establishment errors (requests.exceptions.ConnectTimeout, urllib3.exceptions.NewConnectionError wrapping socket.timeout, or socket.timeout raised during the connect phase) as "connect"; treat read-phase timeouts (requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout, urllib3.exceptions.ReadTimeoutError, or socket.timeout raised while reading the response body) as "read".  
- Exactly where to attach the log extra: in HttpClient.request, at the existing except/timeout-handling sites preserve the current logger name, level, and message text but change the call to include extra={"reason": reason} (e.g. logger.error(existing_msg, exc_info=True, extra={"reason": "connect"})); if the code has a single broad timeout handler, detect/inspect the caught exception to set reason before logging and re-raising.  
- Test structure: extend tests/http_client/test_timeouts.py by adding a parametrized test for ("dns","connect","read") that uses the repository’s existing log-capture helpers; for each case monkeypatch the low-level call used by HttpClient (socket.getaddrinfo -> raise socket.gaierror for dns; the connection/PoolManager/new-connection path -> raise a connect-timeout for connect; the response read path -> raise ReadTimeout or socket.timeout for read), call HttpClient.request, and assert the captured log record has record.reason == expected.  
- Implementation notes: do not change method signatures or public API, do not alter log message text/level/logger name, and place the extra={"reason": ...} only on the log statement(s) that already report the timeout so existing log parsing continues to work.  
- After implementing and extending tests I will run the tests/http_client suite, iterate on any failures, and open the PR titled "Improve timeout error logging in HTTP client" listing the modified tests.
